root_cause.text: xe_vm_madvise_ioctl() in the DRM/XE VM madvise path had an error-handling bug where a failure from check_bo_args_are_sane() jumped to madv_fini instead of the cleanup path that frees madvise_range.vmas, leaking the allocated VMA array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the check_bo_args_are_sane() failure branch from `goto madv_fini;` to `goto free_vmas;`, and adds the `free_vmas:` label containing `kfree(madvise_range.vmas);`, while the commit message explicitly says this fixes a memory leak when `check_bo_args_are_sane()` validation fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix xe_vm_madvise_ioctl error handling to free VMA resources when rejecting invalid input with -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The error-handling branch inside xe_vm_madvise_ioctl was changed so that when the checked condition fails and err is set to -EINVAL, control jumps to the free_vmas label instead of the madv_fini label.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes cleanup flow for that invalid-input/error case so execution performs the cleanup associated with free_vmas before continuing, preventing allocated VMA resources from being skipped during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated error-path label for freeing madvise_range.vmas so cleanup can skip drm_exec_fini when that resource was not set up.
intent_record.what: A new label named free_vmas: was inserted immediately before the kfree(madvise_range.vmas); and madvise_range.vmas = NULL; cleanup block, leaving the existing err_fini: label and surrounding statements otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: This creates an additional jump target for error-handling flow so execution can branch directly to the VMAs cleanup block without first passing through the drm_exec_fini(&exec) path, enabling more precise cleanup sequencing depending on what resources were initialized.

grouping_result.intent: Add a dedicated error-path label for freeing madvise_range.vmas so cleanup can skip drm_exec_fini when that resource was not set up.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix xe_vm_madvise_ioctl error handling so invalid-input and early-failure paths correctly free madvise_range.vmas without invoking drm_exec_fini before it has been initialized.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they correct xe_vm_madvise_ioctl() early error handling so failures before drm_exec initialization free madvise_range.vmas via a dedicated cleanup path instead of jumping to madv_fini and leaking the VMA array.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the full relevant control flow in xe_vm_madvise_ioctl(), including allocation, VMA collection, sanity checking, and cleanup labels, so it is sufficient to determine the leak behavior. The root-cause bug is present in this version because madvise_range.vmas is allocated/filled before the BO sanity check, but the error path for check_bo_args_are_sane() still jumps to `madv_fini` instead of the cleanup path that frees the VMA array. Specifically: `err = get_vmas(vm, &madvise_range);` followed by `if (err || !madvise_range.num_vmas) goto madv_fini;` means `madvise_range.vmas` may now be allocated. Then inside `if (madvise_range.has_bo_vmas)`, on sanity-check failure, the code does `err = -EINVAL; goto madv_fini;`. The only freeing of the VMA array is later at `kfree(madvise_range.vmas); madvise_range.vmas = NULL;` before the `madv_fini:` label. Therefore jumping directly to `madv_fini` skips `kfree(madvise_range.vmas)`, leaking the allocated VMA array. The fix is not present because the failure path does not go through the cleanup section that frees `madvise_range.vmas`.
